dedupe_keys.name: ruhrmobil agent based transport model of the ruhr region

description: ruhrMobil is a regional transport model of the Ruhr area that simulates daily travel and assesses the effects of planned transport measures for about five million inhabitants. It covers all modes, car traffic, public transport, cycling and walking and road freight and commercial traffic, and represents commuter flows, delivery traffic, intermodal trips, parking rules and changes in land use. The population is synthesised with socio-demographic attributes, and each traveller is an agent following an individual daily schedule and choosing modes. The model is built on the open-source MATSim software, with extra modules for commercial traffic, and was developed by TU Berlin under a research contract, with Bergische Universität Wuppertal contributing on freight. The Regionalverband Ruhr launched it in November 2025. Coverage is the Ruhr region of Germany. Access: from 2026 it is to be used in a test phase for regional and municipal projects, offered to interested municipalities; no public release is stated in the press release. Caveats: it is new and in testing, and details of calibration are not given in the source read. It supports agent-based simulation of regional travel and freight, policy and infrastructure appraisal and disruption scenarios, and complements MATSim and the Melbourne MATSim model catalogued here.
